blocks.h2: How an Overhead Sewer System Works
blocks.body: Every drain below the street sewer's flow line, like your floor drain, a basement bathroom, or a laundry line, normally relies on gravity to reach the sewer. An overhead sewer system reroutes those drains into a sump pit instead. An [ejector pump](/chicago-lincoln-park/ejector-pump) lifts that wastewater up to a line above flood level, where a check valve keeps it from flowing back down. From there, gravity carries it the rest of the way to the street sewer, the same as every drain upstairs.

blocks.intro: According to MWRD, two-thirds of an inch of rain in an hour can overwhelm Chicago's combined sewers. In July 2023, the McCook Reservoir filled to capacity.

items.body: Below-grade apartments in two-flats and three-flats are the most exposed spaces in the neighborhood.
Low ceilings and old foundations take careful planning.
A blocked lateral can cause backups too. A [sewer repair](/chicago-lincoln-park/sewer-repair) may be the fix.

blocks.h2: Overhead Sewer Questions From Lincoln Park Homeowners

items.q: Can a garden unit bathroom work with an overhead sewer?
items.answer: Yes. The bathroom, kitchen and floor drains all empty into the new pit, and the pump lifts the wastewater out.

items.preview: A sealed pipe that raises the floor drain opening.
items.answer: A standpipe is a sealed pipe in the floor drain that raises the opening above backup level. It's a simple fix for light backups, but it doesn't protect basement fixtures.

items.q: Does an overhead sewer stop seepage?
items.answer: No. It stops sewer backups. Water seeping through walls or the floor is a groundwater or foundation issue.
Usually a few days, depending on the layout and fixtures.

items.q: Will an overhead sewer work in a condo building?
items.answer: Yes. Because it changes shared plumbing, the association usually approves it.

items.preview: It depends on your basement. You'll approve a flat price first.
